{{nihongo|'''Sunosaki Shrine'''|洲崎神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Awa Province (Chiba)]].

'''Susaki Shrine''' (すさきじんじゃ / すのさきじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Susaki, {{ill|Tateyama, Chiba|ar|تاته ياما (تشيبا)|azb|تاتیاما، چیبا|ce|Татеяма (гӀала)|ceb|Tateyama (lungsod sa Hapon)|cs|Tatejama (město v Čibě)|de|Tateyama (Chiba)|eo|Tatejama (Ĉiba)|es|Tateyama (Chiba)|et|Tateyama|eu|Tateyama (Chiba)|fa|تاته‌یاما، چیبا|fi|Tateyama|fr|Tateyama|gl|Tateyama, Chiba|hu|Tatejama (Csiba)|hy|Տատեյամա|id|Tateyama, Chiba|it|Tateyama|ja|館山市|ko|다테야마시|mg|Tateyama|ms|Tateyama, Chiba|mzn|تاتیاما، چیبا|nl|Tateyama (Chiba)|pl|Tateyama|pt|Tateyama|ro|Tateyama, Chiba|ru|Татеяма (город)|sv|Tateyama|sw|Tateyama, Chiba|tg|Татеяма|th|ทาเตยามะ (จังหวัดชิบะ)|tl|Tateyama, Chiba|tr|Tateyama, Chiba|tt|Татеяма (шәһәр)|uk|Татеяма (Тіба)|ur|تاتییاما، چیبا|uz|Tateyama (Chiba)|vi|Tateyama, Chiba|war|Tateyama, Chiba|zh|館山市|zh_classical|館山市|zh_min_nan|Tateyama-chhī|zh_yue|館山|qid=Q646755}}, {{ill|Chiba Prefecture|Q80011|qid=Q80011}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} (major shrine) {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|Q135022904|qid=Q135022904}}, and during the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}} it was regarded as the {{ill|Ichinomiya|ca|Ichinomiya (Xinto)|de|Ichi-no-miya|fr|Ichi-no-miya|id|Ichinomiya|ja|一宮|ko|이치노미야|pt|Ichinomiya (templo)|simple|Ichinomiya|th|อิจิโนมิยะ|uk|Ітіномія (титул)|zh|一宮|qid=Q1656379}} of {{ill|Awa Province (Chiba)|Q1053044|qid=Q1053044}}. Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=former shrine ranking system}}, it was classified as a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine}}.

The shrine is enshrined on the mid-slope of Mount Mitarai.

=== Enshrined deity ===
The enshrined deity is as follows:
* '''{{ill|Ame no Hiratome|ja|天比理刀咩命|qid=Q85879124|lt=Amahiri-no-Me-no-Mikoto}}''' (あまのひりのめのみこと){{refnest|group="Notes"|The name and reading of the deity follow the “Sanpai no Shiori” distributed by Susaki Shrine.}}
*: She is the consort of {{ill|Awa Shrine|Q705547|qid=Q705547}}’s enshrined deity {{ill|Futodama|Q11059539|qid=Q11059539|lt=Ama-no-Futodama-no-Mikoto}}, and was originally called “Susa no Kami.”

=== Variations in the deity’s name ===
The notation of the deity’s name differs in historical sources as follows:
* Amahiri'''no'''me-no-Mikoto  
*: According to the {{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}} {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Register of Deities}}. Works such as {{ill|Suzuka Tsuratane|Q6536446|qid=Q6536446}}’s {{ill|Jinja Kakuroku|Q11590708|qid=Q11590708}}, the {{ill|Ministry of Religion (Japan)|Q4294653|qid=Q4294653}}-compiled {{ill|Tokusen Jinmyōchō|Q11571092|qid=Q11571092}}, and the “Sanpai no Shiori” distributed by Susaki Shrine follow this notation.
* Amahiri'''to'''me-no-Mikoto (あめのひりとめのみこと)  
*: According to sources older than the Jinmyōchō, such as the {{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|Q1041301|qid=Q1041301}}, {{ill|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|cs|Nihon Montoku Tennó Džicuroku|de|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|es|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|ff|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|fr|Nihon Montoku tennō jitsuroku|ja|日本文徳天皇実録|ko|일본문덕천황실록|pt|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|zh|日本文德天皇實錄|qid=Q1052905}}, and {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}. Documents such as “Susaki Daimyōjin Yui-sho Kyūki” and “Sunomiya Shrine Records” record the deity under this name.
It has been suggested that this discrepancy arose because the Jinmyōchō mistakenly wrote the character “乃” instead of “刀” for the name originally recorded as Amahiritome-no-Mikoto in the {{ill|Rikkokushi|Q1151168|qid=Q1151168|lt=official histories}}<ref name="kamigami">Kenichi Tanigawa (ed.), *Gods of Japan – Shrines and Sacred Sites – Vol. 11 Kantō* (Hakusuisha, December 1984)</ref>.

According to the “Kanemaru Family Genealogical Record” ({{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} 2 [{{ill|1597|Q6790|qid=Q6790}}]), the Sunomiya Kō Shrine in Sunomiya Village, Awa District, later called Sunomiya Myōjin, was regarded as the inner sanctuary and the second shrine, while Susaki Myōjin on Mount Mitarai in Susaki Village was regarded as the worship hall and the first shrine. Based on this, it has been proposed that Susaki Shrine and {{ill|Sunomiya Shrine|Q11556507|qid=Q11556507}} formed a paired shrine complex enshrining the “Susa no Kami,” with Susaki Shrine as the first shrine and Sunomiya Shrine as the second<ref name="kiso">Medieval Provincial Ichinomiya System Research Group (ed.), *Fundamental Research on the Medieval Provincial Ichinomiya System* (Iwata Shoin, February 2000)</ref><ref name="kamigami" />.

=== History ===
=== Founding ===
According to the {{ill|Kogo Shūi|Q531555|qid=Q531555}} ({{ill|Daidō|Q1373191|qid=Q1373191}} 2 [{{ill|807|Q30016|qid=Q30016}}]), {{ill|Amatomi no Mikoto|ja|天富命|qid=Q24899653}}, acting on the orders of {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ar|الإمبراطور جينمو|arz|الامبراطور جينمو|as|জিম্মু|az|Cimmu|bcl|Emperador Jimmu|be|Імператар Дзіму|ca|Jinmu|cdo|Sìng-ū Tiĕng-huòng|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر جینمو|cs|Džimmu|de|Jimmu|el|Αυτοκράτορας Τζίμου|eo|Imperiestro Jinmu|es|Jinmu Tennō|et|Jimmu|eu|Jimmu enperadorea|fa|امپراتور جینمو|fi|Jinmu|fr|Jinmu|hak|Sṳ̀n-vú Thiên-fòng|he|ג'ימו, קיסר יפן|hi|सम्राट जिममु|hr|Jinmu|hu|Dzsinmu japán császár|id|Jimmu|it|Jinmu|ja|神武天皇|jv|Jimmu Tenno|ka|ძიმუ|ko|진무 천황|kw|Emperour Jimmu|la|Jimmu|lt|Imperatorius Džinmu|lv|Džimmu|mn|Эзэн Хаан Жиммү|mr|जिम्मू|ms|Maharaja Jimmu|my|ဂျင်းမူ ဧကရာဇ်|nl|Jimmu|no|Jimmu|pl|Jimmu|pt|Jimmu|ru|Император Дзимму|sh|Car Jimmu|simple|Emperor Jimmu|sl|Cesar Džinmu|sr|Џинму|sv|Jimmu|th|จักรพรรดิจิมมุ|tl|Emperador Jimmu|tr|Jimmu|uk|Імператор Дзімму|uz|Jimmu|vi|Thiên hoàng Jimmu|war|Emperador Jimmu|wuu|神武天皇|zh|神武天皇|zh_classical|神武天皇|zh_min_nan|Sîn-bú Thian-hông|zh_yue|神武天皇|qid=Q200188}}, landed in Awa Province in search of fertile land and developed it. He later led part of the {{ill|Inbe clan|Q8189229|qid=Q8189229}} to the {{ill|Bōsō Peninsula|Q1022115|qid=Q1022115}} in pursuit of even richer land. According to the shrine tradition “Susaki Daimyōjin Yui-sho Kyūki,” compiled in {{ill|Hōreki|Q1194397|qid=Q1194397}} 3 ({{ill|1753|Q7621|qid=Q7621}}), Susaki Shrine originated when Amenotomi-no-Mikoto enshrined a mirror belonging to his ancestral grandmother deity Amahiri-no-Me-no-Mikoto on Mitarasu-yama (Mount Mitarai).

Shrine tradition also recounts that in Yōrō 1 ({{ill|717|ab|717|af|717|am|717 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|717|ar|717|ary|717|ast|717|az|717|azb|۷۱۷ (میلادی)|be|717|be_x_old|717|bg|717|bn|৭১৭|bpy|মারি ৭১৭|br|717|bs|717.|ca|717|cdo|717 nièng|ceb|717|ckb|٧١٧|crh|717|cs|717|cv|717|cy|717|da|717|de|717|el|717|eml|717|eo|717|es|717|et|717|eu|717|fa|۷۱۷ (میلادی)|fi|717|fo|717|fr|717|fy|717|ga|717|gan|717年|gd|717|gl|717|hak|717-ngièn|he|717|hi|717|hr|717.|ht|717 (almanak jilyen)|hu|717|hy|717|id|717|ilo|717|io|717|is|717|it|717|ja|717年|jv|717|ka|717|kaa|717|kk|717 жыл|ko|717년|la|717|lb|717|lij|717|lmo|717|lt|717 m.|lv|717. gads|map_bms|717|mdf|717|mg|717|mhr|717|mk|717|mr|इ.स. ७१७|mrj|717 и|ms|717|mzn|۷۱۷|nah|717|nap|717|nds|717|new|सन् ७१७|nl|717|nn|717|no|717|nrm|717|nso|717|oc|717|or|୭୧୭|os|717-æм аз|pl|717|pnb|717|pt|717|qu|717|ro|717|ru|717 год|rue|717|sa|७१७|scn|717|sd|717ع|sh|717.|shn|717|si|717|sk|717|sl|717|smn|717|sq|717|sr|717|su|717|sv|717|sw|717|tg|Соли 717|th|พ.ศ. 1260|tk|717|tl|717|tly|717|tr|717|tt|717 ел|uk|717|ur|717ء|uz|717|vec|717|vi|717|vls|717|war|717|wuu|717年|xmf|717|zh|717年|zh_min_nan|717 nî|zh_yue|717年|qid=Q23532}}), a great earthquake buried Kanegae Pond within the precincts, and a great serpent guarding a subterranean bell caused calamities. {{ill|En no Gyōja|de|En no Gyōja|es|En no Gyōja|fa|ان نو گیوجا|fr|En no Gyōja|he|אן נו גיוג'ה|it|En no Gyōja|ja|役小角|ko|엔노 오즈누|pl|En-no Gyōja|ru|Эн-но Гёдзя|sh|En no Gyōja|uk|Ен-но-Ґьодзя|zh|役小角|qid=Q198946}} is said to have performed prayers for seven days and nights, received a divine oracle, and subdued the serpent, thereby removing the disaster. It is also said that En no Gyōja placed sacred stones for maritime safety on the shore in front of the beach torii and at Awaguchi Shrine in {{ill|Yokosuka|Q200578|qid=Q200578|lt=Yokosuka}}{{refnest|group="Notes"|The paired sacred stone is enshrined as the sacred object of Awaguchi Shrine in Yoshii, Yokosuka City.}}. These legends indicate that Susaki Shrine was strongly influenced by {{ill|Shugendō|Q1483875|qid=Q1483875}} and {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|Q2279088|qid=Q2279088}} from early times<ref name="kamigami" />.

=== Overview ===
==== Medieval period ====
“Awa Province Amahiritome-no-Kami” appears frequently in the {{ill|Rikkokushi|Q1151168|qid=Q1151168}} and received successive promotions in {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} (see {{ill|Susaki Shrine|ja|洲崎神社|simple|Susaki Shrine|qid=Q11556513|lt=below}}).

In the {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274}} 5 ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}) edition of the Engishiki Jinmyōchō, it is recorded as “Kōshin Amahiri-no-Me-no-Mikoto Shrine, Major, original name Susa-no-Kami” in Awa District, Awa Province, and was ranked as a major shrine. Susaki Shrine is one of the {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|Q135022904|qid=Q135022904}} of this shrine, the other being Sunomiya Shrine, and disputes over which was the true Shikinaisha continued from the Edo period.

In {{ill|Eihō|Q1193881|qid=Q1193881}} 1 ({{ill|1081|Q19450|qid=Q19450}}), the deity’s rank reached the highest level of {{ill|Senior First Rank|Q11123258|qid=Q11123258}}. Later, in {{ill|Kōan (Kamakura period)|Q389180|qid=Q389180}} 4 ({{ill|1281|Q5537|qid=Q5537}}), it was awarded Second Order of Merit for contributions during the {{ill|Mongol invasions of Japan|Q208156|qid=Q208156}}.

In {{ill|Jishō|Q1194671|qid=Q1194671}} 4 ({{ill|1180|Q19702|qid=Q19702}}), {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800|qid=Q242800}} fled by sea to Awa Province after his defeat at the {{ill|Battle of Ishibashiyama|Q2888010|qid=Q2888010}}. According to the {{ill|Azuma Kagami|ckb|ئازوما کاگامی|de|Azuma Kagami|fa|آزوما کاگامی|fr|Azuma kagami|id|Azuma Kagami|ja|吾妻鏡|ko|아즈마카가미|vi|Azuma Kagami|zh|吾妻鏡|qid=Q1042324}}, he visited Susaki Shrine to pray and donated shrine lands in gratitude for safe passage by sea<ref>{{ill|Nirō Aida|Q11582311|qid=Q11582311}}, *Medieval Checkpoints* (Une Shobō, 1943; reprinted by Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 1983)</ref>. On {{ill|Juei|Q598057|qid=Q598057}} 1 ({{ill|1182|Q19708|qid=Q19708}}) August 11, {{ill|Anzai Kageyasu|Q60990454|qid=Q60990454}} was dispatched as an envoy to pray at Susaki Shrine for the safe childbirth of Yoritomo’s wife {{ill|Hōjō Masako|Q463961|qid=Q463961|lt=Masako}}.

The Azuma Kagami also records an order in {{ill|Yōwa|Q729609|qid=Q729609}} 1 ({{ill|1181|Q19704|qid=Q19704}}) to stop disturbances by local officials in shrine lands of Susaki, addressed to Sunomiya Shrine priests, marking the earliest documentary evidence of relations between the two shrines<ref name="kamigami" />.

From ancient times, the shrine collected tolls from passing vessels, indicating control over maritime passage rights and sea checkpoints. This suggests that in the early and mid-medieval periods, Susaki Shrine held the greatest authority and power in Awa Province<ref>Tsuneari Takigawa, “The Satomi Clan of Bōsō and Maritime Transport in Edo Bay,” *Chiba Shigaku* No. 24, 1994</ref>.

==== Edo period ====
In {{ill|Bunka|Q1373146|qid=Q1373146}} 9 ({{ill|1812|Q6933|qid=Q6933}}), the senior councilor {{ill|Matsudaira Sadanobu|Q284038|qid=Q284038}} donated a plaque reading “Awa Province Ichinomiya Susaki Daimyōjin.” Although this plaque served as the basis for identifying the shrine as Ichinomiya, the wording is ambiguous. The designation was later asserted in {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 13 ({{ill|1938|Q18645|qid=Q18645}}), though no historical text formally records it as Ichinomiya. The *History of Tateyama City* suggests this may have been a misunderstanding based on the existence of an Ichinomiya Road in Nishimisaki.

Until the Edo period, the shrine was administered by the bettō temple Yōrō-ji, a situation that continued until the {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} government issued the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|qid=Q1970535|lt=separation of Shinto and Buddhism}} decree in {{ill|1868|Q7717|qid=Q7717}}.

==== Modern era ====
[[File:Susaki Shrine in 1926.jpg|250px|thumb|Around 1926 (Taishō 15)]]
In {{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}}, the Ministry of Doctrine designated Sunomiya Shrine as the Shikinaisha, but reversed this decision the following year and designated Susaki Shrine instead, though the reasoning remains unclear<ref name="kamigami" />. In {{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}, it was ranked as a prefectural shrine under the modern system.

Located at a maritime chokepoint, the shrine maintained a custom until around {{ill|1940|Q18633|qid=Q18633}}–{{ill|1941|Q5231|qid=Q5231}} of collecting offerings from passing ships. In {{ill|1972|Q2476|qid=Q2476}}, Mount Mitarai was designated a Chiba Prefectural Natural Monument as the “Susaki Shrine Natural Forest.” Today, the shrine is managed concurrently, with no resident priests.

=== Divine ranks ===
Chronology of divine ranks for “Amahiri-no-(To)-Me-no-Mikoto”:
* {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|Q1075605|qid=Q1075605}} 9 ({{ill|842|Q24730|qid=Q24730}}) Oct 2: Promoted from no rank to Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade (*Shoku Nihon Kōki*).
* {{ill|Ninju|Q1373077|qid=Q1373077}} 2 ({{ill|852|Q30383|qid=Q30383}}) Aug 22: Promoted to Junior Third Rank (*Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku*).
* {{ill|Ten'an|Q1075611|qid=Q1075611}} 3 ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}) Jan 27: Promoted from Junior Third Rank, Eighth Order of Merit to Senior Third Rank, Eighth Order of Merit (*Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku*).

=== Precincts ===
[[File:Susaki-jinja (Tateyama), honden.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Main hall (Designated Cultural Property of Tateyama City)}}]]
The main hall is a three-bay {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|qid=Q210684}} structure with copper roofing. Shrine tradition dates it to the {{ill|Enpō|Q1145735|qid=Q1145735}} era ({{ill|1673|Q7617|qid=Q7617}}–{{ill|1681|Q7645|qid=Q7645}}), though large-scale repairs occurred after the mid-Edo period. It is designated a Tangible Cultural Property of Tateyama City.

The Zuijin Gate was built during the {{ill|Hōei|Q1145262|qid=Q1145262}} era, and 150 steps lead from behind it to the shrine buildings.

Outside the beach torii stands a rounded stone called the “Sacred Stone,” said to be one of a pair dedicated from the Dragon Palace, the other enshrined at {{ill|Awaguchi Shrine|Q59282598|qid=Q59282598}} on the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|Q536757|qid=Q536757}}. The Awaguchi stone represents “A-gyō,” while the Susaki stone represents “Un-gyō,” together guarding the entrance to Tokyo Bay{{refnest|group="Notes"|Information board.}}.

Because the sea before the shrine is a key maritime route into Tokyo Bay, many votive plaques dedicated by ship captains for safe voyages were once seen before the war.

After the shrine suffered major damage from the {{ill|Typhoon Faxai|Q67170176|qid=Q67170176}} in {{ill|Reiwa era|Q62609017|qid=Q62609017}}, donations were received from various supporters, including the Tokyo talent agency {{ill|Johnny & Associates|Q11728013|qid=Q11728013|lt=Johnny & Associates (then; now SMILE-UP.)}}, and used for reconstruction such as rebuilding torii of the Inari sub-shrine. A commemorative stone expressing gratitude for this support stands within the precincts.

=== Festivals ===
* Early February (Hatsuuma): Offering of the {{ill|Susaki Dance|Q11556509|qid=Q11556509|lt=Susaki Dance}}.
* Grand Festival ({{ill|August 20|Q2824|qid=Q2824}}–{{ill|August 21|Q2823|qid=Q2823}}): Portable shrine procession and Susaki Dance.

=== Cultural properties ===
=== Chiba Prefecture–designated ===
* {{ill|Intangible Folk Cultural Property|Q11406175|qid=Q11406175|lt=Intangible Folk Cultural Property}}
** {{ill|Susaki Minoko Odori|Q11556509|qid=Q11556509}}
**: Consists of Miroku Dance and Kashima Dance. Designated June 9, {{ill|Cerreto Castello|Q18051|qid=Q18051}}.
* {{ill|Natural Monument|Q11406175|qid=Q11406175|lt=Natural Monument}}
** Susaki Shrine Natural Forest
**: A preserved natural forest on Mount Mitarai, designated September 29, {{ill|1972|Q2476|qid=Q2476}}.

=== Tateyama City–designated ===
* Tangible Cultural Properties
** Susaki Shrine Main Hall – designated February 21, {{ill|Canton 10|Q18277|qid=Q18277}}.
** Three documents titled “Susaki Daimyōjin Engi” – designated August 26, {{ill|West Herzegovina Canton|Q18275|qid=Q18275}}.
* Tangible Folk Cultural Property
** Sacred hair – said to be the hair of the enshrined deity Amahiri-no-Me-no-Mikoto.

=== Branch shrines ===
* Underwater branch shrine (within Hasama Underwater Park): Established to pray for prevention of maritime accidents.
* {{ill|Shinagawa Shrine|Q11418419|qid=Q11418419}} ({{ill|Shinagawa|Q233495|qid=Q233495}}, {{ill|Tokyo|Q1490|qid=Q1490}}): Transferred by Minamoto no Yoritomo for maritime safety.
* Edo branch: Said to have been transferred by {{ill|Ōta Dōkan|Q386144|qid=Q386144}} as the guardian deity of Edo.

=== Access ===
'''Address'''
* Susaki 1697, Tateyama City, Chiba Prefecture

'''Transportation'''
* From {{ill|Tateyama Station (Chiba)|Q553883|qid=Q553883}} ({{ill|East Japan Railway Company|Q499071|qid=Q499071}}{{ill|Uchibō Line|Q1142964|qid=Q1142964}})
** Take {{ill|JR Bus|Q1010222|qid=Q1010222}} (Susaki Line) to “Susaki Shrine” stop (about 30 minutes)

'''Nearby'''
* {{ill|Sunosaki Lighthouse|Q1087248|qid=Q1087248}}
* Yajiri Well: About 700 m north of the shrine; associated with a legend of Minamoto no Yoritomo.
